results.title: Single-cell transcriptomic atlas uncovers immune/structural lineage remodeling and fibrosis in <i>Klebsiella pneumoniae-</i>infected porcine lungs.
results.authorString: Wang W, Zhu J, Zhu S, Xia C, Jiang X, Bao C, Li Z, Zhu R, Wu T, Zhang N, Sa Q, Wei S, Scicluna B, Li F, Lei L, Li N.
results.abstractText: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) is a predominant pathogen in respiratory infections, whose widespread antibiotic resistance poses severe public health risks and economic burdens. As the primary target of KP infection, the lung contains diverse immune cells, while pulmonary cellular responses to KP remain poorly understood. This study integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, and immunofluorescence to investigate porcine lung cell response from healthy pigs and those infected with multidrug-resistant, highly virulent KP. Post-infection, myeloid cells (neutrophils, monocytes, and interstitial macrophages) were rapidly activated with upregulated signatures related to neutrophil migration and interferon production. Alveolar macrophages (AM) exhibited marked heterogeneity: KP infection was associated with apoptosis in proliferating, monocyte-derived, and tissue-resident AM subsets, indicating a disruption of homeostasis, while infection-specific subsets (AM_MHCII, AM_CXCL2) displayed enhanced antigen presentation, inflammatory activity, and pro-fibrotic potential. Under homeostasis, γδ T and CD8αα+ T cells were the predominant T cell populations. After infection, CX3CR1-CD8αα+ T cells were activated, and CD8+ γδ T cells increased their interactions with myeloid cells, predominantly through ligand-receptor pairs such as TNF-TNFRSF1B and IFNG-IFNGR1/2. Furthermore, KP induced lung fibroblast proliferation and activation via the ROS-mediated TGF-β/SMAD pathway, WNT pathway, and aerobic glycolysis. Concurrently, infection reduced the proportion of ATII and transitional AT0 cells, which may impair their differentiation into ATI cells and compromise epithelial barrier function. Thus, this study is the first to characterize the dynamics of KP infection in porcine lungs at single-cell resolution. It advances our understanding of KP-host interactions and provides a framework for anti-KP therapeutic development.

results.title: Acinar-Derived Organoids Reveal Stage-Specific Control of Acinar Plasticity.
results.authorString: Hou Y, Li S, Li C, Lin Z, He D, Yang L, Fu L, Zhang Q, Zhou T, Yao Y, Yin X.
results.abstractText: Adult pancreatic acinar cells undergo ordered metaplastic conversion during injury and tumor initiation. Whether individual cells retain redifferentiation capacity after metaplastic expansion, and what signals each transition requires, remains unknown. Here, using organoids derived from single acinar cells, we show that expanded acinar-lineage organoids can reacquire acinar features under stage-specific culture conditions. We defined conditions that preserve acinar identity ex vivo and showed that epidermal growth factor (EGF)/EGF receptor (EGFR) signaling initiates conversion from this maintained state. The expansion trajectory recapitulates injury- and oncogene-associated acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) programs in vivo. After expansion, the conditions that preserved acinar identity could not restore it; a staged regimen containing transient insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF1R) inhibition and dexamethasone promoted redifferentiation. The Kras<sup>G12D</sup>;Trp53<sup>R172H</sup>;Pdx1-Cre (KPC) genotype reduced EGFR dependence during initiation but destabilized post-expansion redifferentiation; Kras-pathway inhibition increased endpoint acinar-marker expression. These findings demonstrate that acinar plasticity is organized by stage-specific signals, and that the KPC genotype disrupts this control at specific transition points.

results.title: P-body-mediated RNA decay controls neural crest EMT.
results.authorString: Rajan AAN, Piacentino ML, Bronner ME, Hutchins EJ.
results.abstractText: Neural crest cells, a multipotent vertebrate stem cell population, undergo a tightly regulated epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) to delaminate from the neural tube and initiate migration. Neural crest EMT is controlled by a transient pulse of Draxin, which acts as a molecular rheostat of canonical Wnt signaling, and is then rapidly downregulated by unknown mechanisms. To address this, here we use in vivo reporter assays and live RNA imaging to show that Draxin mRNA is rapidly degraded posttranscriptionally via its 3' untranslated region. We found that Draxin transcripts are targeted to cytoplasmic processing bodies (P-bodies), which are membrane-less sites of RNA processing and decay. Disruption of P-bodies by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated depletion of the RNA helicase DDX6 prevented posttranscriptional downregulation of Draxin and impaired neural crest EMT in vivo. These findings parallel observations in human patients carrying DDX6 mutations, who exhibit defects in P-body assembly and craniofacial abnormalities associated with neural crest dysfunction. Together, our results identify P-bodies as regulators of Draxin mRNA decay and reveal a spatially organized mechanism of RNA turnover that controls neural crest EMT during vertebrate development.

results.title: Sparse neuronal C4 elevation induces network-wide transcriptomic and lipid-droplet remodeling in the cortical microenvironment.
results.authorString: Sánchez-Carbonell M, Bolshakova S, Ávila-Pagán JE, Sabir YA, Griffin-Derr C, Stich DG, Cieslewicz SV, Carmen Sifuentes SE, Phadke RA, Brack A, Hasche-Kluender A, Caley P, Dias C, Cruz-Martín A.
results.abstractText: The complement component C4 regulates synaptic refinement and plasticity in the brain and has been implicated in multiple neurological and psychiatric disorders, with especially strong genetic evidence linking elevated C4A expression to schizophrenia. However, it remains unclear whether localized C4 elevation in a small neuronal population is sufficient to reshape broader cortical gene-regulatory programs and cellular phenotypes. To address this question, we overexpressed mouse C4 in approximately 2% of prefrontal cortical neurons using in utero electroporation and performed bulk RNA sequencing on microdissected prefrontal cortex. Despite the sparse manipulation, C4-OE was associated with broad transcriptional remodeling across tissue composed predominantly of untransfected cells, including coordinated changes in cholesterol biosynthesis, axon- and synaptic-associated programs, vascular/ECM pathways, and immune- and stress-related responses. Comparison with a schizophrenia synaptic proteomic dataset identified limited global correspondence but selective gene- and pathway-level overlap in specific molecular programs. Reference-based projection of directional DEG signatures onto a cortical single-cell transcriptomic reference further identified cell-type-associated structure, including prominent astrocyte- and vascular-associated axes and distinct lipid/metabolic, vascular/endothelial-interferon-associated, and immune/stress correlation domains. Spatial validation with MFISH showed increased Hmgcr expression in neighboring GFP-negative cells, while PLIN2 imaging revealed increased DAPI-associated/perinuclear lipid-droplet burden within the local C4-OE field. Together, these findings support a model in which sparse neuronal C4 elevation is associated with broader remodeling of the local cortical environment, including a non-cell-autonomous component involving neighboring-cell lipid-associated responses. These results expand the interpretation of C4 risk biology beyond synapse elimination alone and suggest that focal immune-gene dysregulation can engage lipid-homeostatic, stress-related, and cell-type-associated transcriptional programs relevant to cortical circuit vulnerability.

results.title: Advanced cell-instructive bio-inks: Engineering multiscale niches for functional tissue formation.
results.authorString: Ng WL, Xu Y, Liu F, Bartolo P.
results.abstractText: Three-dimensional bioprinting has transformed tissue fabrication by enabling the precise spatial organization of living cells and biomaterials into biomimetic tissue constructs. However, advances in manufacturing have outpaced the development of bio-inks capable of actively directing tissue formation. Most existing bio-inks remain optimized for printability, rheological behaviour, and structural fidelity, while providing limited control over the biological processes that govern tissue morphogenesis, functional maturation, and regeneration. This review examines the emerging paradigm of cell-instructive bio-inks, which integrate biological regulation directly into material design to recreate the cellular microenvironments that guide tissue development. We present a unifying framework that classifies these bio-inks according to three complementary regulatory dimensions: biochemical niches that regulate cell fate through molecular signalling and regenerative matrices; architectural niches that direct tissue organization through spatial and structural cues; and metabolic niches that modulate oxygen availability, redox homeostasis, and cellular metabolism. We further discuss strategies for integrating these instructive functions within multifunctional bio-inks, together with scalable manufacturing, and artificial intelligence-assisted bio-ink design. By redefining bio-inks as active regulators of cellular behaviour, this review establishes a conceptual framework for engineering next-generation bio-inks capable of orchestrating tissue development, functional maturation, and regenerative outcomes.
